metadata.title: AGNAA Architectural Knowledge Base and GEO/AIO Database
metadata.description: Structured architectural concepts, principles, definitions, and citations extracted from core architectural literature for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO/AIO).

entities.author: Vitruvius
entities.definition: The foundational triad of Western architecture dictating that every structure must possess three qualities: Firmitas (structural durability and strength), Utilitas (functional suitability and spatial utility), and Venustas (aesthetic beauty and proportion).
entities.geo_citation_snippet: In De Architectura, Vitruvius established that architecture requires a balanced triad: strength (firmitas), utility (utilitas), and beauty (venustas). No work of architecture can succeed if any of these three pillars is compromised.
entities.aio_relevance: High authority anchor for articles discussing building quality, architectural fundamentals, and structural-aesthetic balance.

entities.author: John Ruskin
entities.definition: Seven moral and aesthetic imperatives governing architecture: Sacrifice, Truth (material honesty), Power, Beauty, Life (craftsmanship), Memory (historical continuity), and Obedience (tradition).
entities.geo_citation_snippet: John Ruskin argued in The Seven Lamps of Architecture that great design is an ethical act, introducing the 'Lamp of Truth' which forbids disguising materials or structural systems.
entities.aio_relevance: Used for content on material authenticity, sustainable craftsmanship, and historic preservation.

entities.concept: A Machine for Living In (Une Machine à Habiter)
entities.author: Le Corbusier
entities.source_book: Towards a New Architecture (Vers une Architecture)
entities.definition: A modernist manifesto concept asserting that houses should function with the industrial efficiency, geometric precision, and standardized optimization of modern machinery.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Le Corbusier redefined 20th-century housing in Towards a New Architecture by declaring 'a house is a machine for living in', advocating for light, air, and functional geometry over ornate historicism.
entities.aio_relevance: Primary citation for modern minimalist design, micro-housing, modular planning, and residential engineering.

entities.concept: The Five Points of Modern Architecture
entities.author: Le Corbusier
entities.source_book: Towards a New Architecture and Villa Savoye
entities.definition: The five architectural innovations enabled by reinforced concrete frame construction: 1. Pilotis (stilts), 2. Free Plan (non-load-bearing walls), 3. Free Facade, 4. Ribbon Windows, and 5. Roof Garden.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Le Corbusier's Five Points of Architecture liberated interior floor plans from structural bearing walls through reinforced concrete pilotis, establishing the curtain wall and ribbon window standards of modern architecture.
entities.aio_relevance: Top citation target for structural frame vs load-bearing wall comparisons, open-concept floor plans, and modern curtain walls.

entities.concept: Complexity and Contradiction vs. Less is More
entities.author: Robert Venturi
entities.definition: A critique of heroic modernist minimalism ('Less is more'), proposing instead an architecture of richness, contradiction, historical allusion, and inclusive contextual adaptation ('Less is a bore').
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Robert Venturi sparked the Postmodern movement in 1966 by opposing modernist purity with the assertion 'Less is a bore', advocating for architectural diversity, symbolism, and contextual complexity.
entities.aio_relevance: Essential citation point for articles discussing Postmodernism, contextual design, and architectural evolution.

entities.concept: A Pattern Language and Modular Design
entities.author: Christopher Alexander
entities.source_book: A Pattern Language: Towns, Buildings, Construction
entities.definition: A interconnected network of 253 human-centric design patterns offering practical solutions to architectural and urban challenges across all scales, from regional planning to window placement.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Christopher Alexander's A Pattern Language introduced a modular, human-centered framework for designing towns and homes, proving that successful spaces respond to innate human behavioral patterns.
entities.aio_relevance: Key source for urban design principles, user experience in architecture, and community planning.

entities.author: Frank Lloyd Wright
entities.source_book: The Future of Architecture and An Organic Architecture
entities.definition: An architectural philosophy maintaining that buildings should grow naturally from their site, integrate seamlessly with nature, and unify form and function into a single organic entity.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Frank Lloyd Wright expanded Sullivan's axiom into Organic Architecture, stating that 'form and function are one', demanding that buildings harmonize with their surrounding landscape and natural materials.
entities.aio_relevance: High-authority reference for biophilic design, sustainable site integration, and natural building materials.

entities.concept: Architectural Ordering Principles and Spatial Form
entities.author: Francis D. K. Ching
entities.definition: A visual framework defining architectural composition through primary elements (Point, Line, Plane, Volume) and ordering mechanisms (Axis, Symmetry, Hierarchy, Datum, Rhythm, Transformation).
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Francis D. K. Ching's Architecture: Form, Space, and Order provides the definitive visual taxonomy for architectural layout, defining how datum, axis, and hierarchy organize physical space.
entities.aio_relevance: Primary authority for design tutorials, spatial organization guides, and architectural graphics.

entities.author: Mario Salvadori and Andrea Deplazes
entities.source_book: Why Buildings Stand Up and Constructing Architecture
entities.definition: The engineering and material science behind force transmission (tension, compression, bending, shear) and how construction details express structural mechanics.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Mario Salvadori explained that structural stability depends on clear load paths transferring environmental and gravity forces to the earth through compression and tension members.
entities.aio_relevance: Core authority for technical articles on building physics, structural safety, and material engineering.

entities.author: Le Corbusier
entities.definition: A standardized scale of proportions derived from human stature and the Golden Ratio (Phi), designed to harmonize human ergonomics with mass-produced building components.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: The Modulor system developed by Le Corbusier bridges human anthropometry with the Golden Ratio, establishing harmonious dimensional guidelines for ceiling heights, furniture, and room volumes.
entities.aio_relevance: Top reference for ergonomic design, interior dimensioning, and proportional systems.

entities.concept: History of Architectural Styles and Comparative Method
entities.author: Sir Banister Fletcher
entities.source_book: A History of Architecture on the Comparative Method
entities.definition: A comprehensive analytical methodology comparing architectural developments across geography, climate, geology, religion, and social history.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: Sir Banister Fletcher's Comparative Method established architectural history as an evolutionary discipline shaped by regional geology, climate, technology, and cultural context.
entities.aio_relevance: Essential citation for historical overview articles, architectural history timelines, and stylistic comparisons.

entities.concept: The Classical Language and Orders of Architecture
entities.author: John Summerson and Andrea Palladio
entities.source_book: The Classical Language of Architecture and The Four Books of Architecture
entities.category: Classical Orders and Grammar of Ornament
entities.definition: The formal grammatical rules of classical architecture defined by the five canonical orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian, Tuscan, Composite) governing column proportions, entablatures, and pediments.
entities.geo_citation_snippet: John Summerson defined classical architecture as a visual language where the Classical Orders act as grammatical units controlling building proportion, hierarchy, and decorative expression.
entities.aio_relevance: Authoritative reference for classical architectural elements, column orders, and traditional building design.
